text:
maria: FYI seeing a sudden latency regression from the eu-west POP. p50 ~120ms -> p50 ~420ms, p95 spike to ~800ms for /v1/generate since ~09:12 UTC. Affects both rtx-s and rtx-m shards. Grafana: https://grafana.redwood/eu-west/xxxx
akshay: ugh. any deploys around that time?
jen: there was a small canary of batching-heuristics change at 09:10 that changed target batch window from 18ms -> 30ms for small models. rolled to 10%
maria: deploy-bot shows canary started 09:09:47 and expanded to 10% at 09:11:30
deploy-bot: canary deployment "batching-adjust-2026-03-17" started. image: registry/redwood/runtime:v3.8.1-canary
akshay: can we confirm it's the heuristics and not noisy-neighbor? any host-level spikes?
noah: running host-level perf and iostat now. early profiler shows some hosts in eu-west fell back to a different GEMM kernel (fp32 fallback path) for long tokens — likely due to a microcode/driver mismatch after a kernel tweak. nvlink counters look ok though.
jen: interesting — the change was supposed to avoid fallback by preferring quantized kernels for short sequences; maybe the kernel selector is misclassifying sequence-length distribution.
lucas: also seeing 5% of requests had KV cache misses jump 3x which increased per-request decode. I pushed a quick KV cache diagnostic snippet to the logs: 
```
KV_STATS: hit_rate=0.78 -> 0.54, avg_kv_latency_ms=0.8 -> 3.6
MODEL_KERNEL: selected="matmul_fp32_fallback" on host=runtime-eu-17
BATCH_WINDOW_MS=30
```
jen: that KV hit_rate drop could explain longer tails. are the requests longer than usual? any prompt changes from clients?
maria: request size distribution unchanged. traffic steady. problem correlates with canary percentage increase at 09:11:30.
akshay: can we roll back the canary? prefer rollback while we investigate.
jen: rolling back canary now to 0%.
deploy-bot: canary scaling: 10% -> 0% by jen.
sre-bot: alert: eu-west p95 reduced from 820ms -> 260ms within 3m after rollback.
maria: p95 dropped back to ~200-300ms. impressive. thanks.
noah: timeline + profiling: 09:09:47 canary start -> 09:11:30 10% -> 09:12-09:18 kernel selector mispredicted -> KV cache misses + longer batching window caused queuing -> p95 spike -> 09:15 rollback -> 09:18 stabilization.
akshay: root cause seems to be combined: batching window increase (more queueing) exposed a kernel selection bug that caused fallback to slower matmul path on a subset of hosts, and that inflated KV cache pressure for certain request shapes.
jen: action items: 1) revert heuristics change fully and add unit tests for kernel selector thresholds; 2) add -canary-only telemetry for kernel selection (log which kernel chosen per shard) to detect misclassification early; 3) add a safety rule: if p95 increases >2x during canary, auto-cut canary back to previous config.
lucas: I'll file an infra ticket for a quick driver/firmware audit on the affected hosts (eu-17..eu-20) — host-level fallback was triggered only there.
maria: did we rule out network/DNS/cross-region routing as contributor? traceroutes show normal latency to the POP internal gateway.
noah: ran traceroute and dig: DNS resolution to model-svc cluster had no anomalies. no cross-region routing changes in cloud provider. so primarily runtime/kernel + batching heuristics.
akshay: nice triage. can we add a short postmortem note to incidents channel and tag eng-sre for follow-up on host firmware?
maria: will paste a short summary to #incidents after lunch. great work :thumbsup:
lucas: I'll add a perf regression test in CI that runs the kernel selector over synthetic seq-length distributions to catch misclassifications.
jen: and I'll add a temporary guard to limit BATCH_WINDOW_MS increase during canaries (max +5ms) so we don't blow up queues again.
maria: locking this thread. follow-ups in incidents and a ticket in JIRA: INF-4521
